editorial:
Imagine living in a world where your favorite music is literally illegal. That is exactly what you get with this story. You follow a group of rebellious teens in Nazi Germany who are obsessed with American swing music. They sneak around to dance and listen to records, creating their own little bubble of joy while the world around them gets darker. The vibe starts off feeling like a fun coming-of-age story, but it quickly turns into a tense struggle as the government starts cracking down on anyone who does not fit in. You will really feel for these kids as they try to hold onto their friendship and their love for music.

The acting is great, especially since the cast is so young, and the music will have you tapping your feet the whole time. The movie does a good job showing how hard it is to stay true to yourself when everyone is telling you to conform. One downside is that it feels a bit like a typical teen movie at times, but the emotional payoff is worth it. You should definitely check it out if you love stories about rebels. If you can, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night.
endingExplained: The story ends on a sad but powerful note. Many of the friends are torn apart by the war and the Nazi regime. Thomas, the main character, has to face the harsh reality that music cannot save everyone from hate. Some characters are sent to camps or forced into the army. It wraps up by showing that while the kids lost their innocence, the spirit of freedom and music lived on through their memories.
toneAndPace: starts upbeat, becomes heavy, steady pace
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about youth rebellion and great music.
